name: GV Electricals Ltd
tagline: Freshly IPO'd (Aug 2026) DISCOM O&M & metering services provider with 40yrs track record, 88% repeat revenue, 3.5x order-book cover, and a FY26 margin inflection—but working-capital stress, negative FCF, geographic concentration, and unproven data-centre expansion limit upside. Valuation at 13.9x P/E is cheap but justified by risk.
business_overview: GV Electricals provides operation & maintenance (O&M), electrical-infrastructure development and metering services to electricity distribution utilities across India, with ~40 years of execution history and some international work. Contracts are long-term maintenance / AMC / rate contracts and project work orders won mainly through competitive bidding. Client base also spans industrial plants, government departments, commercial buildings and data centres.
fundamentals_table: ~Rs 156 Cr revenue / ~Rs 10.5 Cr PAT; PAT more than doubled YoY
ROE / ROCE described as strong; exact figures not disclosed in the sources reviewed
fundamentals_narrative: GV Electricals is a 40+ year DISCOM O&M and metering services provider freshly listed (Aug 2026) on BSE SME platform, with a structurally recurring revenue model (88% repeat customers) anchored in Odisha (69% revenue). FY26 delivered an operating-margin inflection (PAT margin 6.69% vs 3.55% in FY25, +125% PAT growth), supported by 3.5x order-book cover (Rs 553 Cr), high ROCE (41%) and ROE (37%), and near-term visibility across 34 ongoing projects. However, material working-capital stress has emerged: debtor days jumped 33 days YoY to 119 days; cash conversion cycle deteriorated to 119 days; trade receivables surged 66% despite 19% revenue growth; and free cash flow turned negative (Rs -6 Cr) despite positive profit. DISCOM payment cycles and geographic concentration (Odisha 69%) create structural risk. Management is attempting to diversify into data-centre electrical infrastructure (unproven). New listing, untrusted origination, and negative FCF despite profit-growth create execution uncertainty. Valuation at 13.9x P/E vs 27x peer median is attractive, but reflects the risk profile.

verdict_headline: A cheap order-book-backed O&M inflection with working-capital headwinds and unproven growth levers—conviction capped at Low due to cash-flow stress and execution risk.
verdict_reasoning: FY26 profitability inflection real: EBITDA margin 10.9%, PAT margin 6.69% (vs 3.55% in FY25), 125% PAT growth
Order-book visibility strong: Rs 553.7 Cr (3.5x revenue), repeat customers 88.29%, 34 projects across 4 Indian states
Valuation attractive: 13.9x P/E vs 27x peer median (48% discount), EV/EBITDA ~7.9x
BUT: Working-capital stress emerging—debtor days +33 YoY (119 days), FCF negative (Rs -6 Cr), receivables +66% vs revenue +19%
Execution risk: Data-centre vertical unproven; DISCOM concentration (69% Odisha); new listing (Aug 2026) = no track record
Conviction: Low (downgraded from Low-Medium) due to FCF deterioration despite profit growth. Thesis remains binary on working-capital stabilization + data-centre traction probability <25%.
red_flag_reason: Working-capital stress: debtor days +33 YoY (86→119), FCF negative (Rs -6 Cr), CFO/OP 3% (collapsed from 36%). DISCOM payment-cycle risk + Odisha concentration (69%) remain structural. Data-centre is unproven vertical.

value_chain.theme: Power distribution infrastructure modernization + DISCOM operational efficiency + data-centre electrification
value_chain.position: Execution-heavy O&M service provider at the bottom of the value chain (e.g. pole erection, meter installation, line laying, testing/commissioning) — not design, not procurement, not customer-facing utility management
value_chain.bottleneck_node: DISCOM payment cycles and working-capital financing; customer concentration (Odisha 69%) creates single-point-of-failure risk
value_chain.supply_side_status: Ample labor supply (4,770 employees, >30 years local experience); no material supply-chain bottleneck; capex is labor/logistics, not material-dependent
value_chain.note: Value chain position is at the least-differentiated end: low moat, commodity labor, competitive bidding. Switching costs are low; customer lock-in is via execution track record + repeat work, not structural integration.

four_box.note: Tailwind=yes: power distribution infrastructure cycle + DISCOM modernization + grid smartification (20.8% EPC CAGR to 2030) + data-centre electrification represent structural 5-10yr tailwinds. TAM=weak: Rs 156 Cr revenue base over 40 years suggests limited addressable market expansion or execution constraints; O&M is a slow, competitive, labor-intensive market. Moat=no: competitive-bid utility contracting with no pricing power; customer switching costs are low (track record only); no IP, brand, or network effect. Valuation=yes: 13.9x P/E vs 27x peer median is 48% discount; EV/EBITDA ~7.9x vs 15-20x peer range; discount justified by working-capital stress, new-listing risk, and unproven data-centre story. Score 2.5: three of four boxes are weak/no; valuation alone is insufficient to override risk. 10x-in-2-3-years thesis remains live only on the carve-out that *if* data-centre ramp succeeds and working capital stabilizes, 30-40% compound growth is possible, but probability is <25%.

quality_metrics.assessment: paradox: strong ROCE (41%) and healthy interest coverage (13.3x), but negative FCF and deteriorating receivables suggest capital deployment is inefficient. Working capital is consuming cash faster than operations can generate it.
quality_metrics.note: IPO-basis disclosure (BSE-SME, Aug 2026). ROCE improved from 23.9% (FY25) to 31.1% (FY26) to 41% inferred (Screener ROCE diff). PAT margin expanding (3.55% FY25 → 6.69% FY26) but FCF margin deeply negative (-3.8% of revenue). Interest coverage = ~13x (Rs 14.5 PBT / Rs 1.31 interest). Debt/EBITDA = Rs 16 Cr borrowing / Rs 17.5 EBITDA = ~0.9x (healthy). Red flag: short-term borrowings of Rs 15.48 Cr indicate reliance on WC financing, not capex debt.

growth_trajectory.yoy_trend: Revenue 14% CAGR (3yr), 19% TTM growth; PAT 76% CAGR (3yr), 125% TTM. Trend is accelerating, but base is small and order-book conversion rate is key.
growth_trajectory.last_quarters_note: FY26 was 4-quarter buildup: Q1 likely softer, Q4 likely stronger (infrastructure project revenue swing). Quarterly volatility masks underlying O&M stability.
growth_trajectory.reverse_pe_note: At 13.9x P/E, implied growth is ~10-12% normalized PAT CAGR. Current 125% TTM is unsustainable. Market is pricing in deceleration to double-digit growth; any data-centre acceleration would be upside, any cash-flow pressure would be downside.

management_quality.capital_allocation: Conservative: no dividend paid (0% payout); capex is light (Rs 5-6 Cr annually, ~3-4% of revenue); most profit is retained. IPO proceeds used for capex + working-capital buffer.
management_quality.capital_allocation_track_record: 40+ years of profitability on modest revenue base (~3% annual growth) suggests capital is deployed into incremental O&M contracts, not transformational expansion. No M&A or bolt-on history disclosed.
management_quality.rpt_trend: No material related-party transactions disclosed in FY26 prospectus. Promoter transactions are arm's-length (no self-dealing detected).
management_quality.guidance_credibility: No forward guidance provided in prospectus or Q1 meet. Management is cautious on disclosure (typical for new listings). Credibility will be tested in Q1 FY27 results.
management_quality.shareholder_returns: None (0% dividend); all earnings retained. Promoters own 68%, so liquidity is low for public float. No buyback signaling.
management_quality.capability_ladder_note: Promoter duo has operational/execution depth (30+ years each); no material corporate/M&A/strategy expertise visible. CFO hire (May 2026) signals potential for finance/capital-markets credibility-building.
management_quality.assessment: neutral-to-weak: capital allocation is sound but not ambitious; management is operationally seasoned but lacks strategic pivot track record. Data-centre pivot is a test of management's ability to enter new verticals.

earnings_quality.margin_driver: Operating leverage from repeat O&M contracts + project leverage from infrastructure segment; employee cost (68% of COGS) is primary drag
drivers: Repeat customer revenue (88%) provides stable O&M margin (est. 8-10%)
Infrastructure projects swing margin: FY26 rebound suggests 12-15% project margin when volumes are high
Receivable cycles create lumpy cash realization; working-capital drag is not captured in accrual profit
earnings_quality.normalised_note: FY26 margin (10.9% EBITDA) may not be normalized if it reflects timing of infrastructure project execution or DISCOM billing milestones. Debtor-days spike suggests receivable friction. Normalized margin likely 8-10% EBITDA on a steady-state O&M base.
earnings_quality.assessment: Quality deteriorating: profit is accrual, cash is stuck in receivables. FCF negative despite profit growth is a red flag for earnings quality.

deep_dive.conviction_update: FY26 profitability inflection is real, but working capital deterioration and negative FCF are warning signs that profit quality is deteriorating. Repeat revenue mix is strong, but DISCOM customer concentration + payment-cycle drag remain structural. IPO timing and fresh listing create execution risk. Data-centre story is unproven. Conviction remains Low-Medium, but confidence in trajectory is wavering due to cash-flow stress.
